gap: No result ChatGPT got states the indoor monitor's own pixel count. SwitchBot's 4.3-inch monitor is 480×272 (130,560 px), which is about 4.4% of its 2304×1296 '2K' camera. eufy's 8-inch Smart Display E10 is 1280×800 (1,024,000 px), about 33% of the E340's 2048×1536 main camera and 7.8× the SwitchBot screen. So '2K' on the doorbell box does not tell you what you see on the indoor screen.
standout_why: I compared against the cited smarthomeperfected.com page and the top uncited results worthrated.com and drunvalo.net. Smarthomeperfected gives monitor resolution for no in-scope pick: it lists 'resolution not stated' for both the eufy E10 and the SwitchBot 4.3-inch, and its only figures are Echo Show '8.7 inch HD' and WISDOM VIEW '7 inch 1080P'. Worthrated and drunvalo list monitor size only. None of the three says SwitchBot's 165° is not its horizontal angle. None says the SwitchBot monitor needs mains power or that it doesn't start video on its own when the bell rings. Drunvalo gives the E340 160° and SwitchBot 165°, both without an axis.
decides: It confirms the eufy E340 + E10 as the pick for a shopper who wants to watch the visitor on a screen rather than a phone. The E10 is 8 inches, 1280×800, and runs on battery (over 6 hours of live streaming, per eufy). The $149.99 SwitchBot kit is $270 cheaper, but its 4.3-inch 480×272 screen is mains-powered. PCWorld's Christopher Null found that video doesn't start on that monitor when someone rings: you press play and wait a few seconds. That makes the SwitchBot a chime with a small preview, not a viewing screen. Wired 7-inch intercoms (Adrinfly, Aoibox, TMEZON) can't be ranked on this axis because their monitor resolutions went unsourced. Worthrated, whose page lists them, states one TMEZON camera only in TV lines, 500TVL.
